title: Why a Bolton pub has caught the attention of a paranormal enthusiast duo
excerpt: Bolton's Ye Olde Man and Scythe features on Never A Straight Answer's podcast about Britain's most haunted pubs, exploring Civil War history and ghost stories
content:
One of Bolton's most famous pubs has caught the attention of a podcast followed by people across the UK after being highlighted in a special episode about Britain's most haunted pubs.

The Ye Olde Man and Scythe pub recently featured on Never A Straight Answer, a Greater Manchester-based podcast hosted by Gary Duncan and Lee Taylor.

The duo spent almost a decade discussing ghosts, UFOs, conspiracy theories and strange historical mysteries.

The pair have produced more than 300 episodes since launching the show in 2018.

(Image: Google Maps / Street View)

Their latest episode focuses on some of the UK's most haunted pubs, with Bolton's oldest pub making the cut thanks to its links with the English Civil War and long-running ghost stories.

Gary, who lives in Stretford, said: "The Man and Scythe is really interesting because there's so much history to it.

"It's one of the oldest pubs in the country and there's so much that's happened there."

The pub is famously associated with James Stanley, the 7th Earl of Derby, who is said to have spent his final hours there before being executed outside in 1651.

Taylor is a voice on the podcast (Image: Gary Duncan)

It was also connected to the events surrounding the Bolton Massacre of 1644, one of the bloodiest episodes in the town's history.

Gary said it was the combination of documented history and reported paranormal activity that attracted the podcast's attention.

He said: "There have been reports of hooded figures, flickering lights, objects moving and all sorts of things over the years.

"Usually I'm the sceptic on the show, but on this one I was actually leaning more towards the believer side because there is so much history there."

(Image: Gary Duncan)

The podcast's format revolves around debate between sceptic and believer viewpoints.

Gary explained: "Taylor is more of the believer and I'm the sceptic. We don't try to convince anybody.

"We just present the information and ask people what they think."

Away from ghost stories, the podcast has covered everything from alleged UFO sightings and famous conspiracy theories to historical mysteries and fringe science topics.

(Image: Gary Duncan)

Despite spending years discussing the paranormal, Gary says he remains unconvinced by most claims.

However, Bolton's historic pub left a strong impression.

He said: "The historical context makes it far more plausible than a lot of the stories we look at."

For Bolton residents, the episode is another reminder that the Man and Scythe continues to attract interest far beyond the town itself.

And whether listeners believe in ghosts or not, few would argue with the pub's remarkable place in Bolton's history.
